action: Xbike and Arriva users: treat your email address and trip history as potentially exposed and watch for phishing; Arriva says it is investigating whether anyone besides the researcher requested the data.
date_note: Security.nl published on 19 November; the article gives no date for the flaw itself.
exec: A bike-share platform's access-control flaw exposed users' emails and trips; Arriva says misuse cannot be ruled out.
impact: Email addresses and cycling trips of Xbike users; according to Security.nl, nearly 130,000 people have used the app at least once, of whom more than 40,000 are Arriva customers.
plain: A researcher could pull other users' email addresses and bike trips from the Xbike bike-share app, which Arriva uses. Arriva took the app offline and is investigating.
summary: Security.nl reports, citing NOS, that a researcher could obtain the email address and cycling trips of all Xbike users because all users had rights to request other users' data. Arriva told NOS that protective measures were switched off by mistake and that misuse cannot be ruled out. Arriva took the app offline as a precaution.
title: Arriva investigates possible data leak from Xbike bike-share app

validation.note: Security.nl read; it relays NOS (not read by CyberView).

review.note: Impact said the researcher's downloaded data showed the 130,000 figure; Security.nl only states it; reworded. Title, cause, Arriva statement, offline, status checked
